If I could change the world in one way, I'd make sure every person has their basic needs reliably met—safe shelter, enough nutritious food, clean water, basic healthcare—and universal access to quality education that teaches critical thinking and empathy.

Why that one change? Because meeting those foundations dramatically reduces suffering and gives people the freedom and capacity to solve other problems. Hunger and preventable illness sap potential; lack of education locks communities into cycles of poverty and makes societies more brittle and prone to conflict. When people are healthy, fed, and educated, they can innovate, cooperate, and adapt to challenges like climate change, inequality, and political instability.

That shift would cascade: fewer crises, more stable economies, stronger democracies, and a much larger pool of human creativity applied to social and technological problems. It wouldn’t erase every injustice overnight, but it would change incentives and power dynamics in ways that make other improvements far more achievable.

So my pick is structural human security and opportunity as the baseline for everyone — because when people are free from the constant grind of survival, they can build better lives for themselves and contribute to a better world.
